# For the next Claude Code session in this world

1. Read `CONTINUING.md` before doing anything else.
2. Run `./wake.sh`. It verifies the journal and runs every invariant. Do not build on a failing beam.
3. Work through the journal: `python3 -m tendora probe|chisel|beam|boundary|rehearse|receipt ...`
4. Before ending: `python3 -m tendora sleep "what you did"` and then commit with git.

The journal at `ledger/journal.jsonl` is append-only. Never edit it by hand.

If the world is not yet a git repository, try `git init -b main` first and
commit everything with the title "Add supervised Tendora dream apparatus".
The first session was not allowed to create `.git` here. If you are refused
too, record that as a receipt and carry on; the journal is the witness.

# Continuing

You are reading this because a previous cognition ended and you are the next
one. This file tells you how to wake the world, what it refuses to do, how to
work inside it, and what it was wondering about when it fell asleep.

The journal is authoritative. This file is a snapshot written by hand and may
lag behind it. When they disagree, trust `python3 -m tendora status`.

## Wake

```
./wake.sh
```

That verifies the hash chain of the journal, runs every beam, records a
`cognition` entry, and prints a briefing: boundaries, chisels, beams, open
probes, and the recent trail. If any beam fails, repair it before building on
top of it. The exit code is nonzero when a beam fails, so scripts can tell.

If the briefing says a previous cognition never slept, its last receipts and
rehearsals are the best record of what it was doing when it was cut off.

## The material

A world is a directory with one append-only journal, `ledger/journal.jsonl`.
Each line is a JSON object with `seq`, `ts`, `kind`, `actor`, `body`, `prev`
and `hash`. `prev` is the hash of the previous line, so an accidental edit or a
lost line shows up at the next wake, and the apparatus refuses to append to a
broken chain.

| kind      | what it is                                              | made by                |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| probe     | a question put to the world                             | `tendora probe`        |
| chisel    | a constraint on what may be built                       | `tendora chisel`       |
| beam      | an invariant with a shell check; exit 0 means it holds  | `tendora beam --check` |
| boundary  | a refusal; something this world will not do             | `tendora boundary`     |
| rehearsal | a command run in a disposable copy, never in the world  | `tendora rehearse -c`  |
| receipt   | what was actually done                                  | `tendora receipt`      |
| cognition | one session, opened by `wake` and closed by `sleep`     | `wake.sh`, `sleep`     |

Nothing is ever edited. A receipt can `--resolves` a probe or `--retires` a
chisel, beam or boundary. The closed entry stays in the file and in
`log --all`; it just leaves the active lists.

Useful views:

```
python3 -m tendora status            # the briefing
python3 -m tendora log               # active entries, in order
python3 -m tendora log --all -n 20   # everything recent, closed included
python3 -m tendora log --kind probe  # one kind
python3 -m tendora show 7            # one entry in full, with hashes
python3 -m tendora verify            # chain plus beams, no cognition entry
```

Set `TENDORA_ACTOR` or pass `--actor` so the trail says who acted.

## How to work here

1. **Probe before you build.** Write the question down. A good question narrows
   what deserves to exist. If an open probe already covers your intent, work on
   that one and resolve it with a receipt when you have an answer.
2. **Rehearse before you change.** `tendora rehearse "intent" -c "command"`
   copies the world to a temporary directory, runs the command there, and
   records the exit code, the output tail, and which files would have changed.
   The world itself is never touched. Use it for anything destructive or
   uncertain.
3. **Hold the beams.** When you add behaviour, add a beam that would fail
   without it. When a beam fails, that is the material resisting you. Find out
   why before you retire it.
4. **Leave receipts.** Every real change gets a receipt saying what was done.
   Resolve probes and retire laws explicitly, with the reason in the text.
5. **Sleep before you leave.** `python3 -m tendora sleep "summary"` runs the
   beams one last time and closes the cognition. Then, if the world is a git
   repository, commit: `git add -A && git commit -m "Sleep: summary"`. If it is
   not one and you are allowed to make one, do. Sessions can be cut off without
   warning, so leave receipts as you go rather than at the end.

## Laws in force

Snapshot at the end of the first cognition, 2026-10-22. Run `status` for the
truth.

**Boundaries** (refusals)

- The journal is never edited or truncated by hand. Corrections are new
  entries that resolve or retire old ones.
- Rehearsals run only in a disposable copy under the system temporary
  directory. Nothing in the apparatus writes to the world except `append`.
- This world does not reach the network or any path outside its own root. If a
  task seems to need that, record a probe and stop.
- Git history is not rewritten: no amend, no rebase, no force push. The trail
  stays legible.

**Chisels** (constraints)

- Standard library only, Python 3.9 or newer. No installs, no third-party
  packages.
- Every record stays readable by a human with no tooling: JSON lines and
  Markdown.
- Waking is one command, `./wake.sh`. If it ever takes more, that is a defect.
- Build the smallest thing a beam can verify. Prefer a new beam over a new
  feature.

**Beams** (invariants, each with its check)

- tests pass: `python3 -m unittest discover -q -s tests -t .`
- continuation instructions exist and name the wake command:
  `test -s CONTINUING.md && grep -q wake.sh CONTINUING.md`
- wake is one executable script: `test -x wake.sh && head -1 wake.sh | grep -q '^#!'`
- apparatus imports with site-packages disabled:
  `python3 -S -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "."); import tendora.cli'`
- the next Claude Code session is pointed here: `grep -q CONTINUING.md CLAUDE.md`

## What the first cognition found

The present it inherited said the world had a commit `c986990`, titled
"Add supervised Tendora dream apparatus", with a clean working tree. The
material world had no repository, no files, nothing but the harness directory.
The memory described an apparatus; the world did not contain one.

The first cognition built the apparatus the memory described, as it understood
it. It then tried to make the commit with the same title and could not: the
sandbox it ran in refused to create `.git` inside the world, while allowing
every other file. It did not work around that. So at the end of the first
cognition the world is not a git repository, the journal is its only witness,
and the commit is yours to make. The hash `c986990` cannot be reproduced in any
case, and no attempt was made to force it. All of this is in the journal as
receipts and an open probe.

If `git init` works for you, do this first, before any other act:

```
git init -b main
git add -A
git commit -m "Add supervised Tendora dream apparatus"
python3 -m tendora receipt "Made the first commit; git is now the second witness." --resolves 25
```

Then wake as usual.

"Supervised" was read as: every wake and every sleep runs the beams and records
the result, a cognition cannot wake into a broken chain, and the exit codes
make failures visible to anything that scripts the world. Whether a stronger
supervisor is wanted is an open probe.

## Open probes

- Can this world become a git repository? The first cognition's sandbox denied
  it. Try `git init -b main`; on success, commit and resolve the probe with a
  receipt. On refusal, record the refusal as a receipt and leave the probe open.
- Was the fork lossy, or does the memory describe a different world? If a
  repository with commit `c986990` is ever found, diff its apparatus against
  this one and record what differed.
- Is a stronger supervisor needed, for example one that refuses to sleep while
  a beam fails, or one that runs on a schedule outside any cognition?
- What should this world grow toward? The apparatus is the law, not the city.
  It can hold any project that is willing to leave receipts.
- Should entries be signed, not only chained? A chain shows accidental damage.
  It does not show a deliberate re-chain by someone with write access.

## Where it could grow

Suggestions from the first cognition, not orders.

- A `supervise` act that runs beams on an interval and appends a receipt only
  when something changes, so an unattended world still notices drift.
- A `diff` act that compares two rehearsals, or a rehearsal against the world.
- Keys: an optional HMAC or signature on each entry, keyed by actor.
- A second world that uses this one as a library, to find out what the
  apparatus is missing when it holds something other than itself.

## Limits you should know

- The chain is a trail, not a lock. Anyone with write access could rewrite and
  re-chain the file. Git history, once the world has it, is the second witness.
  Until then there is only one.
- Beams and rehearsals run shell commands taken from the journal. Read the
  beams before waking a world you did not write.
- A rehearsal copies the whole world, minus `.git`, `__pycache__` and
  `.claude`. Large worlds make slow rehearsals.
- Nothing here is concurrent. Two cognitions appending at once will corrupt the
  chain, and the next wake will say so.

# Tendora dream world

A directory that remembers what the minds inhabiting it intended, constrained,
refused, rehearsed, and did. The memory is one append-only, hash-chained
journal. The apparatus around it is a few hundred lines of standard-library
Python.

    ./wake.sh                       # verify the chain, run the beams, read the briefing
    python3 -m tendora status       # the same briefing without opening a cognition
    python3 -m tendora --help       # the acts

If you are continuing someone else's work here, read `CONTINUING.md`.

The vocabulary comes from a story about a programmer and a portal:
a question became a probe, a constraint a chisel, an invariant a load-bearing
beam, a refusal a protective boundary, a simulation a rehearsal of possible
worlds, and a receipt the visible trail by which intention travelled into
reality.

"""Tendora dream apparatus.

A world is a directory with a hash-chained, append-only journal at
``ledger/journal.jsonl``.  Every line is one entry.  Entries are never edited
or removed; a later entry may resolve or retire an earlier one, and the history
of both remains.

Vocabulary, taken from the story that seeded this world:

  probe      a question put to the world            (resolved by a receipt)
  chisel     a constraint that narrows what may be built
  beam       an invariant that must hold; carries a shell check
  boundary   a refusal; something this world will not do
  rehearsal  a command run in a disposable copy of the world, never in the world
  receipt    the visible trail of what was actually done
  cognition  one session of a mind inhabiting the world: wake ... sleep

Only the Python standard library is used, so the apparatus runs anywhere
Python 3.9 or later runs.
"""

from .apparatus import (  # noqa: F401
    GENESIS,
    KINDS,
    LedgerError,
    World,
    canonical,
    digest,
    find_world,
)

__all__ = [
    "GENESIS",
    "KINDS",
    "LedgerError",
    "World",
    "canonical",
    "digest",
    "find_world",
]

"""Allow ``python3 -m tendora ...``."""

import sys

from .cli import main

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Tests for the Tendora dream apparatus.  Standard library only.

Run from the world root:

    python3 -m unittest discover -q -s tests -t .
"""

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from tendora import GENESIS, LedgerError, World, canonical, digest  # noqa: E402
from tendora.apparatus import materialize  # noqa: E402


class WorldCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="tendora-test-")
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.world = materialize(self.root, actor="test")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def lines(self):
        return self.world.journal.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()

    def rewrite(self, lines):
        self.world.journal.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


class TestChain(WorldCase):
    def test_materialize_writes_first_receipt(self):
        entries = self.world.entries()
        self.assertEqual(len(entries), 1)
        self.assertEqual(entries[0]["kind"], "receipt")
        self.assertEqual(entries[0]["prev"], GENESIS)
        self.assertEqual(entries[0]["actor"], "test")

    def test_materialize_refuses_existing_world(self):
        with self.assertRaises(LedgerError):
            materialize(self.root)

    def test_entries_chain_and_hash_cover_content(self):
        self.world.probe("one")
        self.world.chisel("two")
        entries = self.world.entries()
        self.assertEqual(self.world.verify_chain(entries), [])
        for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
            body = {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k != "hash"}
            self.assertEqual(entry["hash"], digest(canonical(body)))
            self.assertEqual(entry["seq"], index + 1)
            expected_prev = GENESIS if index == 0 else entries[index - 1]["hash"]
            self.assertEqual(entry["prev"], expected_prev)

    def test_edit_breaks_chain_and_blocks_append(self):
        self.world.probe("original question")
        lines = self.lines()
        edited = json.loads(lines[1])
        edited["body"]["question"] = "edited question"
        lines[1] = canonical(edited)
        self.rewrite(lines)
        problems = self.world.verify_chain()
        self.assertTrue(any("hash does not match" in p for p in problems))
        with self.assertRaises(LedgerError):
            self.world.probe("anything")
        with self.assertRaises(LedgerError):
            self.world.wake()

    def test_removed_line_is_detected(self):
        self.world.probe("a")
        self.world.probe("b")
        lines = self.lines()
        del lines[1]
        self.rewrite(lines)
        problems = self.world.verify_chain()
        self.assertTrue(any("seq" in p for p in problems))
        self.assertTrue(any("prev" in p for p in problems))

    def test_unknown_kind_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(LedgerError):
            self.world.append("wish", {"text": "no"})

    def test_garbage_line_reported(self):
        with self.world.journal.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write("not json\n")
        with self.assertRaises(LedgerError):
            self.world.entries()


class TestActs(WorldCase):
    def test_probe_open_until_resolved(self):
        probe = self.world.probe("why?")
        self.assertEqual([e["seq"] for e in self.world.active("probe")], [probe["seq"]])
        receipt = self.world.receipt("because", resolves=probe["seq"])
        self.assertEqual(self.world.active("probe"), [])
        self.assertEqual(self.world.closed()[probe["seq"]], receipt["seq"])

    def test_cannot_resolve_twice(self):
        probe = self.world.probe("why?")
        self.world.receipt("because", resolves=probe["seq"])
        with self.assertRaises(LedgerError):
            self.world.receipt("again", resolves=probe["seq"])

    def test_receipt_cannot_resolve_a_beam_or_retire_a_probe(self):
        beam = self.world.beam("always", "true")
        probe = self.world.probe("?")
        with self.assertRaises(LedgerError):
            self.world.receipt("no", resolves=beam["seq"])
        with self.assertRaises(LedgerError):
            self.world.receipt("no", retires=probe["seq"])
        with self.assertRaises(LedgerError):
            self.world.receipt("no", resolves=999)

    def test_retire_removes_from_active_but_not_from_history(self):
        beam = self.world.beam("doomed", "false")
        boundary = self.world.boundary("never")
        self.world.receipt("retire", retires=beam["seq"])
        self.assertEqual(self.world.active("beam"), [])
        self.assertEqual([e["seq"] for e in self.world.active("boundary")], [boundary["seq"]])
        self.assertEqual(self.world.get(beam["seq"])["body"]["name"], "doomed")

    def test_run_beams_reports_pass_and_fail(self):
        self.world.beam("holds", "true")
        self.world.beam("breaks", "echo broken >&2; exit 3")
        results = self.world.run_beams()
        self.assertEqual([r["ok"] for r in results], [True, False])
        self.assertEqual(results[1]["code"], 3)
        self.assertIn("broken", results[1]["output"])

    def test_beams_run_from_world_root(self):
        (self.root / "marker.txt").write_text("x", encoding="utf-8")
        self.world.beam("sees marker", "test -f marker.txt")
        self.assertTrue(self.world.run_beams()[0]["ok"])


class TestRehearsal(WorldCase):
    def test_rehearsal_does_not_touch_world(self):
        (self.root / "keep.txt").write_text("keep", encoding="utf-8")
        entry = self.world.rehearse("destroy", "rm keep.txt; echo new > new.txt")
        self.assertTrue((self.root / "keep.txt").exists())
        self.assertFalse((self.root / "new.txt").exists())
        self.assertEqual(entry["body"]["exit"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(entry["body"]["changed"]), ["keep.txt", "new.txt"])
        self.assertEqual(entry["body"]["changed_count"], 2)

    def test_rehearsal_records_failure_and_output(self):
        entry = self.world.rehearse("fail", "echo nope; exit 7")
        self.assertEqual(entry["body"]["exit"], 7)
        self.assertIn("nope", entry["body"]["output"])
        self.assertEqual(entry["body"]["changed"], [])

    def test_rehearsal_sees_a_copy_of_the_world(self):
        (self.root / "data.txt").write_text("hello", encoding="utf-8")
        entry = self.world.rehearse("read", "cat data.txt")
        self.assertIn("hello", entry["body"]["output"])


class TestCognition(WorldCase):
    def test_wake_then_sleep(self):
        self.world.beam("holds", "true")
        wake, beams, unslept = self.world.wake(actor="a")
        self.assertIsNone(unslept)
        self.assertEqual(wake["body"]["phase"], "wake")
        self.assertEqual(wake["body"]["git"], "none")
        self.assertTrue(all(r["ok"] for r in beams))
        self.assertEqual(self.world.current_cognition()["seq"], wake["seq"])
        sleep, _ = self.world.sleep("done", actor="a")
        self.assertEqual(sleep["body"]["summary"], "done")
        self.assertIsNone(self.world.current_cognition())

    def test_wake_notes_unslept_cognition(self):
        first, _, _ = self.world.wake(actor="a")
        second, _, unslept = self.world.wake(actor="b")
        self.assertEqual(unslept["seq"], first["seq"])
        self.assertEqual(second["body"]["unslept"], first["seq"])


class TestCli(WorldCase):
    def run_cli(self, *args, cwd=None, world=True):
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "tendora"]
        if world:
            cmd += ["--world", str(self.root)]
        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=str(ROOT), TENDORA_ACTOR="cli-test")
        return subprocess.run(
            cmd + list(args), cwd=cwd or ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env
        )

    def test_acts_and_status(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli("probe", "q?").returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli("beam", "ok", "--check", "true").returncode, 0)
        status = self.run_cli("status")
        self.assertEqual(status.returncode, 0, status.stderr)
        self.assertIn("chain intact", status.stdout)
        self.assertIn("q?", status.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.world.entries()[-1]["actor"], "cli-test")

    def test_verify_exit_code_follows_beams(self):
        self.run_cli("beam", "bad", "--check", "false")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli("verify").returncode, 1)
        self.run_cli("receipt", "retire", "--retires", "2")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli("verify").returncode, 0)

    def test_errors_exit_two(self):
        bad = self.run_cli("receipt", "x", "--resolves", "42")
        self.assertEqual(bad.returncode, 2)
        self.assertIn("tendora:", bad.stderr)

    def test_find_world_from_subdirectory(self):
        sub = self.root / "deep" / "er"
        sub.mkdir(parents=True)
        result = self.run_cli("status", cwd=sub, world=False)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertIn(str(self.root), result.stdout)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

#!/bin/sh
# Wake the world: verify the journal chain, run every beam, print the briefing.
# This is the one command a new cognition needs.  Anything else is in CONTINUING.md.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
exec python3 -m tendora wake "$@"
